Yes. For your goal, I’d look for someone who understands fitness marketing + beginner psychology, rather than a generic social-media manager.

A few Toronto-area options stood out:

The Influence Agency — full-service Toronto agency covering social, paid media, SEO, email, branding and web. Better if you want content tied into a broader acquisition strategy.

Qode Social Media Agency — particularly relevant if you need content creation, social copy, photography/videography and ongoing social strategy.

Jasmine Williams Media — a smaller Toronto content/copywriting consultancy. Their process includes voice-of-customer research, which is useful for figuring out exactly what makes nervous beginners hesitate.

Writing Web Words Inc. — Toronto/North York copywriting and SEO content agency; potentially useful for rewriting your website/trial landing page around beginner objections.

Create Content Canada — Toronto content-marketing consultancy focused on positioning, audience understanding and consistent multi-channel content.

There are also fitness-specific agencies worth considering even if they're not Toronto-based. Red Leaf, for example, explicitly works with gyms and fitness businesses on content designed to build confidence before a first visit, trial offers and the customer journey from online discovery to booking. 
Red Leaf Media
 Growsooner similarly recommends beginner education, trainer videos, member proof, facility walkthroughs and FAQ-style content because beginners often can't tell what their first visit will actually be like. 
Growsooner

What I'd actually hire them to create

I'd brief them around “make the first visit feel familiar before they arrive.” For example:

“What happens when you book a trial?” — 30–60 second walkthrough.

“I haven't worked out in years. Can I still come?” — coach answers on camera.

“What should I wear/bring?”

“Will everyone be fitter than me?”

“What happens when I walk through the door?”

Beginner member stories — especially people who were initially intimidated.

Meet your coach — personality, coaching style, what they won't do.

First-class walkthrough — parking → entrance → changing → warm-up → workout → leaving.

Trial FAQs — price, commitment, cancellation, fitness level, class size.

Low-pressure CTA: “Come try one session. We'll show you what to do.”

That's supported by what successful Toronto gyms are already emphasizing: for example, Empact explicitly addresses “I haven't trained in a while,” intimidation and being judged, while Fuel highlights modifications for every ability level. 
Empact
+1

My shortlist: If you want content itself, I'd start with Jasmine Williams Media or Qode. If you want content + the whole trial-booking funnel, I'd look at Red Leaf or The Influence Agency.

If you tell me your gym's neighbourhood, type of training (e.g. CrossFit, strength, boxing, personal training), and target beginner, I can search specifically for agencies/freelancers with relevant fitness case studies and narrow it to 3–5 people.

ChatGPT can make mistakes. Check important info.
